What you will learn

  • Set up optional BYOK safely and understand its costs.
  • Inspect preview, timeline, Stop, Continue and session-only history.

Before you begin

A disposable CodeC project. For live requests: provider eligibility, your own key, network and willingness to incur charges. A no-key reading path is included.

Optional means optional

You can finish every non-AI exercise without an AI key. CodeC does not host a model or pay for requests. Gemini is the default; NVIDIA Build is a separate manual dev/test option, not silent fallback. Read provider data boundaries before sending code.

  1. Use a disposable project with only your own non-sensitive code. Open the AI rail slot → AI home.
  2. Choose Google Gemini (default). Obtain your own key using the app’s Get a key link. NVIDIA Build is a separate, manual dev/test-only option.
  3. Read the selected provider’s data-use terms and the 18+/terms confirmation. Save the key in CodeC, never on this website or in source files. Your key pays the provider’s bill.
  4. Optionally tap Test connection: it sends a fixed one-word request, no code. It is still a network request.
  5. Open chat and read Before you ask; choose I understand — start when ready. This agreement is not an Android permission.

Keys are encrypted with Android Keystore in no_backup/ai, not stored in the project or its backup. The app’s key-acquisition links lead to the provider. Never paste a real key into this website, an example file or a bug report.

A complete first question

Create the following hello.c in an otherwise harmless project. Read it yourself before asking the model to explain it.

hello.c for the AI exercise

#include <stdio.h>
int main(void) {
    puts("Hello, CodeC!");
    puts("I review before I run.");
    return 0;
}

Question to type

Explain what this hello.c program prints. Do not propose changes or run anything.

Expected program output—not a guaranteed AI answer

Hello, CodeC!
I review before I run.

A useful answer explains puts and the two lines. It may phrase things differently or be wrong. Compare it with the source and, if you choose, compile/run using Chapter 2’s commands. An explanation is not a test pass.

The preview is the request

  1. Open Ask about the project or use the relevant selection/question action. Enter the small question.
  2. Read Check before sending: provider, model, exact system instruction and user text. Cancel if a private file or unexpected context appears.
  3. Tap Send only after review. Read the stream and expand a timeline row to see exact tool-result text.

A project task can perform scoped read-only follow-ups after Send and transmit admitted text without another tap for every file. Stop cancels the request; usage already incurred may still be billed. Continue makes a new exact preview and needs Send. One visible pre-text rate retry may occur; it is cancelable.

An agreement is not an invisible grant

Before you ask names small work, your bill/rate limits, reviewing edits yourself and responsibility for code you choose to run. Accepting it reveals the composer; it does not remove Apply/Run approval doors. Merely reading an answer changes no file.

Markdown code blocks have a Copy action, not a hidden execute action. HTTPS links show a confirmation dialog with the full URL. Read it before leaving the app.

Use history without mistaking it for a backup

The chat header’s drawer shows Pinned/Recents, a current marker, pin/unpin and New chat with a confirmation. Up to 20 conversations per project live in memory; follow-ups carry up to 8 turns. Closing/killing the app clears session history. Saving a key does not save raw chat.

Chapter 19 distinguishes bounded persisted task memory/undo from D6 raw chat. No on-device model or autonomous background agent is promised.

Use this table to explain what you would cancel if sensitive context appeared. These are textual teaching states, not a fabricated model conversation or screenshot.

Try it yourself

  1. With a key, ask about a harmless small loop and inspect the preview; without one, write down exactly which context you would permit. Expected: a named provider and reviewed text, not blind trust.
  2. Open a timeline row and compare the result with your source. Try New chat and observe confirmation; do not assume it made a backup.
  3. Optionally press Stop during a live request. Expected: cancellation, not a refund promise or guaranteed zero usage.

Common mistakes

  • Do not equate a saved key with saved conversation history.
  • AI output may be wrong; compare it with source and real output.
  • Send is task-level consent for bounded follow-up reads, not a fresh prompt for every read.
